idea-plugin.name: Phaenon
idea-plugin.description:
Support for Phaenon source files (.phn): a typed dialect of PHP that compiles to PHP.

A Phaenon file is PHP code from the first byte: no <?php open tag, no inline HTML, strict_types implied. In PhpStorm (or any IDE with the PHP plugin) this plugin plugs .phn files into the real PHP lexer, parser and PSI, starting the lexer in code mode, so highlighting, completion, navigation, refactorings and inspections work exactly as they do for PHP. Classes declared in .phn files are indexed and resolvable from PHP files and vice versa.

Without the PHP plugin, a bundled TextMate grammar still provides syntax highlighting.

Source and issues: github.com/phaenonlang/jetbrains. The compiler and the language: github.com/phaenonlang.
idea-plugin.change-notes: 0.2.0: a .phn file is PHP to PhpStorm, so its lexer, parser, indexes and inspections run on it; Phaenon's syntax (generics, list<T>, map<K, V>, tuples, class<T>, closure types, expression bodies and throws, concurrently and spawn, PHP 8.6's partial application) is erased on the way to the parser and its types are given back to completion, navigation, quick documentation and the inspections. In the commercial IDEs the compiler's diagnostics come from phn lsp, which also builds on save; Reformat Code writes Phaenon's layout through phn fmt; and the line map every compiled file carries takes Xdebug's breakpoints, frames and steps, and every position in compiled code a console or a test run shows, to the .phn line.
